# Evidence e1; success=true

# Install and load power analysis package
if (!require("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  library("pwr")
}

# Parameters
mean_increase <- 0.2  # units
sd <- 0.5              # units
cohens_d <- mean_increase / sd  # Effect size
alpha <- 0.05          # Significance level (one-sided)
target_power <- 0.80   # Target power

cat("=== One-Sample t-Test Power Analysis ===\n")
cat("Mean increase (effect):", mean_increase, "units\n")
cat("Standard deviation:", sd, "units\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", cohens_d, "(small to medium)\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test for one-sample t-test
# type = "one.sample", alternative = "greater" for one-sided upper-tail test
result <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,                    # Solve for n
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"      # One-sided upper-tail test
)

cat("Continuous solution (pwr::pwr.t.test):\n")
print(result)

# Extract and round up to minimum integer
n_continuous <- result$n
n_integer <- ceiling(n_continuous)

cat("\n=== Sample Size Determination ===\n")
cat("Continuous solution: n =", n_continuous, "participants\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size: n =", n_integer, "participants\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at n_integer
power_at_selected <- pwr.t.test(
  n = n_integer,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = NULL,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

cat("Verification at n =", n_integer, ":\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_at_selected$power, 6), "\n\n")

# Check power at preceding integer (n_integer - 1)
if (n_integer > 1) {
  power_preceding <- pwr.t.test(
    n = n_integer - 1,
    d = cohens_d,
    sig.level = alpha,
    power = NULL,
    type = "one.sample",
    alternative = "greater"
  )
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_integer - 1, "):\n")
  cat("Achieved power:", round(power_preceding$power, 6), "\n\n")
} else {
  cat("No preceding design (n = 1 is minimum).\n\n")
}

# Summary for structured reporting
results_summary <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_integer,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

cat("=== Structured Results ===\n")
print(results_summary)

# Export as JSON for result marker
library("jsonlite")
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_total")
  ),
  simulation = NULL
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

plan.estimand: Group-by-time interaction effect in repeated-measures ANOVA
plan.hypothesis: Testing for a non-zero group-by-time interaction effect
assumptions: Multivariate normal data
Compound symmetry correlation structure with r=0.5
Sphericity assumption satisfied (epsilon=1)
Balanced design with equal allocation to two groups
No missing data
Univariate F-test for group-by-time interaction
clarification_questions: Confirm: the partial eta-squared of 0.06 is the unadjusted effect size before correlation adjustment, and we should apply the correlation adjustment factor in our power calculation?
Confirm: the univariate F-test approach uses the Greenhouse-Geisser or similar correction, or should we apply unadjusted univariate power with epsilon=1 (no correction needed)?
scientific_notes: For repeated-measures ANOVA, the non-centrality parameter depends on the effect size, number of time points, correlation structure, and sample size
With compound symmetry r=0.5 and k=3 time points, the effective numerator denominator must account for the correlated observations
Sphericity epsilon=1 indicates the assumption holds, so no Greenhouse-Geisser correction is applied to degrees of freedom
G*Power provides adjusted effect sizes for repeated measures; the partial eta-squared adjustment factor is typically f_adjusted = sqrt(eta_sq / ((1-eta_sq) * (1-r) * (k-1)))
The interaction uses df_numerator = (k-1)*(g-1) = 2*1 = 2 degrees of freedom for 3 time points and 2 groups

plan.estimand: omnibus F-test effect in a one-way ANOVA with 3 groups
plan.hypothesis: H0: all group means are equal; H1: at least one group mean differs (population η² = 0.08)
assumptions: Fixed effects one-way ANOVA with 3 independent groups
Balanced design: 25 participants per group
Observations are independent normal random variables
Common variance across all groups (homogeneity of variance)
Population η² = 0.08 defines the non-centrality structure
Omnibus F-test at two-tailed α = 0.05
scientific_notes: Omnibus F-test: H0 states all group means equal; H1 at least one differs
Effect size quantified by η² = Var(group means) / σ²_pooled; related to f = √(η²/(1-η²))

# Balanced one-way ANOVA power calculation
# Design: 3 independent groups, total N = 75, balanced
# Effect size: population eta-squared = 0.08
# Significance level: alpha = 0.05

# Parameters
k <- 3  # number of groups
N <- 75  # total sample size
n_per_group <- N / k  # balanced allocation
eta_sq <- 0.08  # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level

# Verify balanced design
cat("Study Design:\n")
cat("Number of groups (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Total sample size (N):", N, "\n")
cat("Per-group sample size (n):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio: 1:1:1 (balanced)\n")
cat("Population eta-squared (η²):", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n\n")

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f (ANOVA effect size)
# f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²))
f <- sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
cat("Converted to ANOVA effect size f:", f, "\n\n")

# Non-centrality parameter
# λ = f * sqrt(N)
lambda <- f * sqrt(N)
cat("Non-centrality parameter (λ = f√N):", lambda, "\n\n")

# Degrees of freedom
df1 <- k - 1  # numerator df (between groups)
df2 <- N - k  # denominator df (within groups)
cat("Degrees of freedom:\n")
cat("  Numerator (between groups):", df1, "\n")
cat("  Denominator (within groups):", df2, "\n\n")

# Critical value from central F distribution
F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
cat("Critical F-value at α =", alpha, ":", F_crit, "\n\n")

# Power: Pr(F > F_crit | H1 is true)
# Using non-central F distribution with non-centrality λ
power <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)

cat("Power (Pr(reject H0 | H1 true)):", power, "\n\n")

# Report results
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = round(power, 15),
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("Results:\n")
print(results)

# Output in required format
library(jsonlite)
output <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )
)

plan.estimand: Population eta-squared (effect size for omnibus F test in one-way ANOVA)
plan.hypothesis: Omnibus null hypothesis: all three group means are equal. Alternative: at least one group mean differs.
assumptions: Balanced design: equal sample size n per group
Three independent groups with normal distributions
Common variance (homogeneity of variance)
Fixed effects model
Population eta-squared η² = 0.06 reflects the effect size
Omnibus F test with k=3 groups
scientific_notes: Eta-squared converts to noncentrality parameter λ via the relationship with f (Cohen's effect size): f² = η² / (1 - η²), so f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²))
Noncentrality parameter: λ = f × sqrt(N) where N is total sample size
The F distribution has numerator df = k - 1 = 2 and denominator df = N - k = 3n - 3
Inversion will find the minimum integer n per group satisfying power ≥ 0.80
Report achieved power at the selected design and the preceding admissible design

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups, common variance, and population eta-squared = 0.06, the minimum sample size per group required to achieve 80% power at alpha = 0.05 for the omnibus F test is 52 participants per group (156 total participants). The continuous solution was 51.33 participants per group. At n=52, achieved power is 80.56%; at the preceding design (n=51), power is 79.73%, confirming that n=52 is the minimum integer meeting the power requirement.
answer.method: One-way ANOVA sample size inversion using pwr.anova.test() (R package pwr v1.3-0). Eta-squared (η² = 0.06) was converted to Cohen's f via f = √(η²/(1-η²)) = 0.2526. The function inverts the non-central F distribution with numerator df = k-1 = 2 and denominator df = N-k = 3n-3 to find n satisfying the power equation. The continuous solution was rounded up to the nearest integer and verified at both selected and preceding integer designs.

Three independent groups with normal distributions

Omnibus F test for the null hypothesis that all three group means are equal
Type I error rate: alpha = 0.05
No missing data or attrition
limitations: Sample size calculation assumes fixed effects ANOVA; random or mixed effects models require different approaches
Power calculation is based on asymptotic non-central F distribution theory
Homogeneity of variance assumption; violations could affect actual Type I error rate and power
Effect size (eta-squared) must be accurately specified; misspecification invalidates the calculation

# One-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Design: 3 groups, balanced, common variance
# Population eta-squared = 0.06
# Target power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05

# Install/load required package for power analysis
if (!require("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org/")
  library("pwr")
}

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3  # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# f = sqrt(f²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("Effect size conversion:\n")
cat("  eta-squared (η²):", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("  f²:", f_squared, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", f, "\n\n")

# Use pwr.anova.test() to find the minimum n per group
# This function uses the non-centrality parameter approach
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,          # number of groups
  f = f,          # effect size (Cohen's f)
  sig.level = alpha,  # significance level
  power = target_power  # target power
)

n_per_group_continuous <- result$n
power_at_continuous <- result$power

cat("Continuous solution from pwr.anova.test():\n")
cat("  n per group:", n_per_group_continuous, "\n")
cat("  power:", power_at_continuous, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer to ensure power ≥ target
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("Rounded integer solution:\n")
cat("  n per group:", n_per_group, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the selected design (n = ceiling result)
result_selected <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_per_group,
  f = f,
  sig.level = alpha
)

power_selected <- result_selected$power

cat("Power at selected design (n =", n_per_group, "):\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", power_selected, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the preceding design (n - 1)
n_preceding <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_preceding >= 2) {  # minimum sensible sample size
  result_preceding <- pwr.anova.test(
    k = k,
    n = n_preceding,
    f = f,
    sig.level = alpha
  )
  power_preceding <- result_preceding$power
  
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_preceding, "):\n")
  cat("  Power:", power_preceding, "\n\n")
} else {
  power_preceding <- NA
  cat("Preceding design not available (would be n < 2)\n\n")
}

# Summary
cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", k * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (numerator):", k - 1, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (denominator):", k * n_per_group - k, "\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(
      metric = "sample_size",
      value = n_per_group,
      unit = "participants_per_group"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_sample_size",
      value = k * n_per_group,
      unit = "participants"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power_at_selected_design",
      value = round(power_selected, 4),
      unit = "probability"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power_at_preceding_design",
      value = if(!is.na(power_preceding)) round(power_preceding, 4) else NA,
      unit = "probability"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "cohens_f",
      value = round(f, 4),
      unit = "unitless"
    )
  )
)

cat("\nJSON output:\n")
print(jsonlite::toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Independent verification of one-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Using direct non-centrality parameter and F-distribution approach

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3                    # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05            # significance level
target_power <- 0.80

# Step 1: Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# η² = f² × (k - 1) / (1 + f² × (k - 1)) is one relationship
# But the standard formula is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("=== EFFECT SIZE CONVERSION ===\n")
cat("η² = ", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("f² = η² / (1 - η²) = ", eta_squared, " / ", 1 - eta_squared, " = ", f_squared, "\n")
cat("f = sqrt(f²) = ", f, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Verify the relationship between η² and f in ANOVA context
# For ANOVA, η² = SS_between / SS_total
# Cohen's f is defined as f = sqrt(SS_between / SS_within)
# The relationship is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# This is correctly applied in the candidate answer.

# Step 3: Test using base R and non-central F distribution
# For a given n per group:
# - Total sample size N = k × n
# - Numerator df: df1 = k - 1 = 2
# - Denominator df: df2 = N - k = k(n - 1) = 3n - 3
# - Noncentrality parameter: λ = f × sqrt(N) = f × sqrt(k × n)

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n per group
compute_power_anova <- function(n_per_group, k, f, alpha) {
  N <- k * n_per_group
  df1 <- k - 1
  df2 <- N - k
  lambda <- f * sqrt(N)
  
  # Critical F value for the given alpha
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
  
  # Power = P(F > F_crit | H1 true)
  # Under H1, F follows non-central F distribution with noncentrality λ
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(power = power, lambda = lambda, df1 = df1, df2 = df2))
}

# Test at n = 52
result_52 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 52, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 52 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 52, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ = f × sqrt(N) = ", f, " × sqrt(", 3*52, ") = ", result_52$lambda, "\n")
cat("df1 = ", result_52$df1, ", df2 = ", result_52$df2, "\n")
cat("Power at n=52: ", result_52$power, "\n\n")

# Test at n = 51
result_51 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 51, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 51 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 51, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ = f × sqrt(N) = ", f, " × sqrt(", 3*51, ") = ", result_51$lambda, "\n")
cat("df1 = ", result_51$df1, ", df2 = ", result_51$df2, "\n")
cat("Power at n=51: ", result_51$power, "\n\n")

# Test at n = 50
result_50 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 50, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 50 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 50, "\n")
cat("Power at n=50: ", result_50$power, "\n\n")

# Verify: n=52 should give power ≥ 0.80, and n=51 should give power < 0.80
cat("=== VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat("Does n=52 achieve target power 0.80? ", result_52$power >= 0.80, "\n")
cat("Does n=51 fall short of target power 0.80? ", result_51$power < 0.80, "\n")

# Compare with candidate answer
cat("\n=== COMPARISON WITH CANDIDATE ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Candidate reported power at n=52: 0.8055643919819825\n")
cat("Independent computation at n=52: ", result_52$power, "\n")
cat("Difference: ", abs(result_52$power - 0.8055643919819825), "\n\n")

cat("Candidate reported power at n=51: 0.7972572678090943\n")
cat("Independent computation at n=51: ", result_51$power, "\n")

    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n51", value = result_51$power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n50", value = result_50$power, unit = "probability"),

  )),

)

# One-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Design: 3 groups, balanced, common variance
# Population eta-squared = 0.06
# Target power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05

# Install/load required package for power analysis
if (!require("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org/")
  library("pwr")
}

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3  # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# f = sqrt(f²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("Effect size conversion:\n")
cat("  eta-squared (η²):", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("  f²:", f_squared, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", f, "\n\n")

# Use pwr.anova.test() to find the minimum n per group
# This function uses the non-centrality parameter approach
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,          # number of groups
  f = f,          # effect size (Cohen's f)
  sig.level = alpha,  # significance level
  power = target_power  # target power
)

n_per_group_continuous <- result$n
power_at_continuous <- result$power

cat("Continuous solution from pwr.anova.test():\n")
cat("  n per group:", n_per_group_continuous, "\n")
cat("  power:", power_at_continuous, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer to ensure power ≥ target
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("Rounded integer solution:\n")
cat("  n per group:", n_per_group, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the selected design (n = ceiling result)
result_selected <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_per_group,
  f = f,
  sig.level = alpha
)

power_selected <- result_selected$power

cat("Power at selected design (n =", n_per_group, "):\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", power_selected, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the preceding design (n - 1)
n_preceding <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_preceding >= 2) {  # minimum sensible sample size
  result_preceding <- pwr.anova.test(
    k = k,
    n = n_preceding,
    f = f,
    sig.level = alpha
  )
  power_preceding <- result_preceding$power
  
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_preceding, "):\n")
  cat("  Power:", power_preceding, "\n\n")
} else {
  power_preceding <- NA
  cat("Preceding design not available (would be n < 2)\n\n")
}

# Summary
cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", k * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (numerator):", k - 1, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (denominator):", k * n_per_group - k, "\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT

    list(
      metric = "sample_size",
      value = n_per_group,
      unit = "participants_per_group"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_sample_size",
      value = k * n_per_group,
      unit = "participants"

# Independent verification of one-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Using direct non-centrality parameter and F-distribution approach

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3                    # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05            # significance level
target_power <- 0.80

# Step 1: Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# η² = f² × (k - 1) / (1 + f² × (k - 1)) is one relationship
# But the standard formula is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("=== EFFECT SIZE CONVERSION ===\n")
cat("η² = ", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("f² = η² / (1 - η²) = ", eta_squared, " / ", 1 - eta_squared, " = ", f_squared, "\n")
cat("f = sqrt(f²) = ", f, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Verify the relationship between η² and f in ANOVA context
# For ANOVA, η² = SS_between / SS_total
# Cohen's f is defined as f = sqrt(SS_between / SS_within)
# The relationship is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# This is correctly applied in the candidate answer.

# Step 3: Test using base R and non-central F distribution
# For a given n per group:
# - Total sample size N = k × n
# - Numerator df: df1 = k - 1 = 2
# - Denominator df: df2 = N - k = k(n - 1) = 3n - 3
# - Noncentrality parameter: λ = f × sqrt(N) = f × sqrt(k × n)

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n per group
compute_power_anova <- function(n_per_group, k, f, alpha) {
  N <- k * n_per_group
  df1 <- k - 1
  df2 <- N - k
  lambda <- f * sqrt(N)
  
  # Critical F value for the given alpha
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
  
  # Power = P(F > F_crit | H1 true)
  # Under H1, F follows non-central F distribution with noncentrality λ
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(power = power, lambda = lambda, df1 = df1, df2 = df2))
}

# Test at n = 52
result_52 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 52, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 52 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 52, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ = f × sqrt(N) = ", f, " × sqrt(", 3*52, ") = ", result_52$lambda, "\n")
cat("df1 = ", result_52$df1, ", df2 = ", result_52$df2, "\n")
cat("Power at n=52: ", result_52$power, "\n\n")

# Test at n = 51
result_51 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 51, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 51 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 51, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ = f × sqrt(N) = ", f, " × sqrt(", 3*51, ") = ", result_51$lambda, "\n")
cat("df1 = ", result_51$df1, ", df2 = ", result_51$df2, "\n")
cat("Power at n=51: ", result_51$power, "\n\n")

# Test at n = 50
result_50 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 50, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 50 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 50, "\n")
cat("Power at n=50: ", result_50$power, "\n\n")

cat("Does n=51 fall short of target power 0.80? ", result_51$power < 0.80, "\n")

cat("Independent computation at n=52: ", result_52$power, "\n")

cat("Candidate reported power at n=51: 0.7972572678090943\n")
cat("Independent computation at n=51: ", result_51$power, "\n")

# Final result
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n52", value = result_52$power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n51", value = result_51$power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n50", value = result_50$power, unit = "probability"),

  )),

)

# One-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Design: 3 groups, balanced, common variance
# Population eta-squared = 0.06
# Target power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05

# Install/load required package for power analysis
if (!require("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org/")
  library("pwr")
}

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3  # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# f = sqrt(f²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("Effect size conversion:\n")

cat("  f²:", f_squared, "\n")

  sig.level = alpha,  # significance level
  power = target_power  # target power
)

function (k = NULL, n = NULL, f = NULL, sig.level = 0.05, power = NULL)

        1)  
        stop("exactly one of k, n, f, power, and sig.level must be NULL") 
    if (!is.null(f)) { 
        if (is.character(f))  
            f <- cohen.ES(test = "anov", size = f)$effect.size 
        if (any(f < 0))  
            stop("f must be positive") 
    } 
    if (!is.null(k) && any(k < 2))  
        stop("number of groups must be at least 2") 
    if (!is.null(n) && any(n < 2))  
        stop("number of observations in each group must be at least 2") 
    if (!is.null(sig.level) && !is.numeric(sig.level) || any(0 >  
        sig.level | sig.level > 1))  
        stop(sQuote("sig.level"), " must be numeric in [0, 1]") 
    if (!is.null(power) && !is.numeric(power) || any(0 > power |  
        power > 1))

    p.body <- quote({ 
        lambda <- k * n * f^2 
        pf(qf(sig.level, k - 1, (n - 1) * k, lower = FALSE),  
            k - 1, (n - 1) * k, lambda, lower = FALSE) 
    }) 
    if (is.null(power))  
        power <- eval(p.body) 
    else if (is.null(k))  
        k <- uniroot(function(k) eval(p.body) - power, c(2 +

    else if (is.null(n))

    else stop("internal error")

    METHOD <- "Balanced one-way analysis of variance power calculation" 
    structure(list(k = k, n = n, f = f, sig.level = sig.level,  
        power = power, note = NOTE, method = METHOD), class = "power.htest")

answer.summary: For a one-sided one-sample t test with 25 participants, detecting a mean increase of 0.2 units with standard deviation 0.5 units at significance level α = 0.05, the statistical power is 0.6173 (approximately 61.73%).
answer.method: Analytical power calculation using the non-central t distribution. Under the alternative hypothesis that the true population mean difference is 0.2 units, the test statistic T = X̄/(s/√n) follows a non-central t distribution with degrees of freedom = 24 and non-centrality parameter λ = (Cohen's d) × √n = 0.4 × 5 = 2.0. Power is computed as P(T > t₀.₀₅,₂₄) = P(T > 1.7109) under this non-central distribution, verified by three independent computational methods (pwr package, direct non-central t integration, and lower-tail probability complement).

limitations: Power is conditional on the normality assumption; actual power may differ if the outcome is substantially non-normal

One-sided test has lower power than the equivalent two-sided test; committing to direction a priori is required to achieve this power
Calculation assumes the sample mean and variance are unbiased estimators of the population parameters

# One-sample t test power calculation
# Hypothesis: one-sided test (upper tail)
# H0: mu = 0
# H1: mu > 0
# Effect to detect: 0.2 units
# Standard deviation: 0.5 units
# Sample size: 25 participants
# Significance level: 0.05, one-sided

# Parameters
n <- 25
effect_size_raw <- 0.2  # mean difference in original units
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
df <- n - 1  # degrees of freedom for one-sample t test

# Standardized effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- effect_size_raw / sd

# Non-centrality parameter for t distribution
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)

# Under H1, the test statistic follows non-central t distribution
power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp)

                         alternative = "greater", type = "one.sample")$power

# Repeated-measures within-group ANOVA power calculation
# Following G*Power's rm_within design specification

# User-specified parameters
partial_eta_sq <- 0.08
k <- 3  # number of time points
rho <- 0.5  # compound symmetry correlation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
epsilon <- 1  # sphericity assumption satisfied

# Step 1: Convert partial eta-squared to f
# f^2 = eta^2 / (1 - eta^2)
f_sq <- partial_eta_sq / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f <- sqrt(f_sq)

cat("Effect Size Conversion:\n")
cat(sprintf("Partial η² = %.4f\n", partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("f² = η²/(1−η²) = %.4f/(%.4f) = %.6f\n", partial_eta_sq, 1-partial_eta_sq, f_sq))
cat(sprintf("f = √(f²) = %.6f\n\n", f))

# Step 2: Define the noncentral parameter formula
# In G*Power's rm_within ANOVA: λ = f² × n × (k − 1) × (1 − ρ)
# df1 = k - 1 = 2
# df2 = (k - 1) × (n - 1) = 2 × (n - 1)

# Step 3: Function to calculate power for given n
calc_power <- function(n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha) {
  df1 <- k - 1
  df2 <- (k - 1) * (n - 1)
  
  # Noncentral parameter (accounting for correlation structure)
  lambda <- f_sq * n * (k - 1) * (1 - rho)
  
  # Critical F value at alpha
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | H1) = 1 - CDF(f_crit; df1, df2, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  
  return(list(n = n, power = power, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, lambda = lambda, f_crit = f_crit))
}

# Step 4: Find minimum sample size via binary search and exhaustive check
cat("Searching for minimum sample size achieving target power ≥ 0.90:\n\n")

# Start with a reasonable range
n_min <- 1
n_max <- 500

results_table <- data.frame()

# Test values from 1 to 200 to find the crossing point
for (n in 1:200) {
  result <- calc_power(n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
  results_table <- rbind(results_table, data.frame(
    n = n,
    power = result$power,
    df1 = result$df1,
    df2 = result$df2,
    lambda = result$lambda
  ))
  
  if (n <= 20 || n %% 10 == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("n=%3d: power=%.6f, df1=%d, df2=%3d, λ=%.6f\n", 
                n, result$power, result$df1, result$df2, result$lambda))
  }
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_idx <- which(results_table$power >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- results_table$n[min_idx]
achieved_power <- results_table$power[min_idx]

cat("\n" %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "\n")
cat(sprintf("MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE: n = %d participants\n", min_n))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at n=%d: %.6f (%.4f%%)\n", min_n, achieved_power, achieved_power*100))

# Verify the preceding design
if (min_n > 1) {
  prev_result <- calc_power(min_n - 1, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
  cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d (preceding): %.6f (%.4f%%)\n", min_n-1, prev_result$power, prev_result$power*100))
}

cat("="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "\n\n")

# Final verification with detailed computation
final_result <- calc_power(min_n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
cat("Final Verification (n = " %+% min_n %+% "):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Partial η² = %.6f\n", partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("  f = %.6f\n", f))
cat(sprintf("  k (time points) = %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  ρ (compound symmetry) = %.4f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("  df₁ = k − 1 = %d\n", final_result$df1))
cat(sprintf("  df₂ = (k − 1)(n − 1) = %d\n", final_result$df2))
cat(sprintf("  λ = f² × n × (k − 1) × (1 − ρ) = %.6f\n", final_result$lambda))
cat(sprintf("  Critical F (α=0.05) = %.6f\n", final_result$f_crit))
cat(sprintf("  Power (1 − β) = %.6f\n\n", final_result$power))

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(achieved_power, 6), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_n_minus_1", value = round(prev_result$power, 6), unit = "probability")
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

# Repeated-measures within-group ANOVA power calculation
# Following G*Power's rm_within design specification

# User-specified parameters
partial_eta_sq <- 0.08
k <- 3  # number of time points
rho <- 0.5  # compound symmetry correlation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
epsilon <- 1  # sphericity assumption satisfied

# Step 1: Convert partial eta-squared to f
# f^2 = eta^2 / (1 - eta^2)
f_sq <- partial_eta_sq / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f <- sqrt(f_sq)

cat("Effect Size Conversion:\n")
cat(sprintf("Partial η² = %.4f\n", partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("f² = η²/(1−η²) = %.4f/(%.4f) = %.6f\n", partial_eta_sq, 1-partial_eta_sq, f_sq))
cat(sprintf("f = √(f²) = %.6f\n\n", f))

# Step 2: Define the noncentral parameter formula
# In G*Power's rm_within ANOVA: λ = f² × n × (k − 1) × (1 − ρ)
# df1 = k - 1 = 2
# df2 = (k - 1) × (n - 1) = 2 × (n - 1)

# Step 3: Function to calculate power for given n
calc_power <- function(n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha) {
  df1 <- k - 1
  df2 <- (k - 1) * (n - 1)
  
  # Noncentral parameter (accounting for correlation structure)
  lambda <- f_sq * n * (k - 1) * (1 - rho)
  
  # Critical F value at alpha
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | H1) = 1 - CDF(f_crit; df1, df2, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  
  return(list(n = n, power = power, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, lambda = lambda, f_crit = f_crit))
}

# Step 4: Find minimum sample size via binary search and exhaustive check
cat("Searching for minimum sample size achieving target power ≥ 0.90:\n\n")

# Start with a reasonable range
n_min <- 1
n_max <- 500

results_table <- data.frame()

# Test values from 1 to 200 to find the crossing point
for (n in 1:200) {
  result <- calc_power(n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
  results_table <- rbind(results_table, data.frame(
    n = n,
    power = result$power,
    df1 = result$df1,
    df2 = result$df2,
    lambda = result$lambda
  ))
  
  if (n <= 20 || n %% 10 == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("n=%3d: power=%.6f, df1=%d, df2=%3d, λ=%.6f\n", 
                n, result$power, result$df1, result$df2, result$lambda))
  }
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_idx <- which(results_table$power >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- results_table$n[min_idx]
achieved_power <- results_table$power[min_idx]

cat("\n" %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "\n")
cat(sprintf("MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE: n = %d participants\n", min_n))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at n=%d: %.6f (%.4f%%)\n", min_n, achieved_power, achieved_power*100))

# Verify the preceding design
if (min_n > 1) {
  prev_result <- calc_power(min_n - 1, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
  cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d (preceding): %.6f (%.4f%%)\n", min_n-1, prev_result$power, prev_result$power*100))
}

cat("="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "\n\n")

# Final verification with detailed computation
final_result <- calc_power(min_n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
cat("Final Verification (n = " %+% min_n %+% "):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Partial η² = %.6f\n", partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("  f = %.6f\n", f))
cat(sprintf("  k (time points) = %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  ρ (compound symmetry) = %.4f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("  df₁ = k − 1 = %d\n", final_result$df1))
cat(sprintf("  df₂ = (k − 1)(n − 1) = %d\n", final_result$df2))
cat(sprintf("  λ = f² × n × (k − 1) × (1 − ρ) = %.6f\n", final_result$lambda))
cat(sprintf("  Critical F (α=0.05) = %.6f\n", final_result$f_crit))
cat(sprintf("  Power (1 − β) = %.6f\n\n", final_result$power))

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(achieved_power, 6), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_n_minus_1", value = round(prev_result$power, 6), unit = "probability")
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

Normal distribution within each group
Homogeneity of variance (common population variance across groups)
Fixed effects model
Population eta-squared = 0.06
Omnibus F-test is two-sided upper-tail test (standard for ANOVA)
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) is the proportion of total variance explained by group differences
For ANOVA, eta-squared relates to the noncentrality parameter λ through: λ = n*k*η²/(1-η²), where n is per-group sample size and k is the number of groups
The F-distribution for power calculation has numerator df = k-1 and denominator df = k(n-1)
Effect size interpretation: η² = 0.06 is conventionally considered a small to medium effect (Cohen's f ≈ 0.247)

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way fixed effects ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups, common variance, and population eta-squared = 0.06, the minimum sample size to achieve 80% power at significance level α = 0.05 for the omnibus F-test is **52 participants per group** (156 total). The exact solution is 51.33 participants per group; rounding up to the nearest integer yields 52 per group with achieved power of 80.56%, which exceeds the target. The preceding integer (51 per group) yields power of 79.73%, falling short of the 80% target.
answer.method: Analytic power calculation using the F-distribution via pwr::pwr.anova.test() (R package pwr v1.3-0), which implements the noncentrality parameter method for balanced one-way ANOVA. The effect size was converted from population eta-squared (0.06) to Cohen's f (0.2526) using the standard formula f = √[η²/(1−η²)]. The test is two-sided upper-tail with numerator df = k−1 = 2 and denominator df = k(n−1) = 153 at the selected design. Sample size was determined by finding the smallest integer n such that power ≥ 0.80.
assumptions: Three independent groups with equal sample sizes per group (balanced design)
Normal distribution within each group
Homogeneity of variance (common population variance across all groups)
Fixed effects model
Population eta-squared = 0.06
Omnibus F-test with upper-tail critical region at α = 0.05
No missing data or attrition
Allocation ratio 1:1:1
limitations: The calculation assumes no practical constraints on recruitment or data collection; attrition was not modeled and was not requested
Effect size specification (η² = 0.06) is assumed known; sensitivity to misspecification was not explored
The analytic solution assumes adequacy of large-sample approximation at n = 52 per group; finite-sample departures from normal theory were not formally assessed
Omnibus test power does not guarantee power for post-hoc pairwise comparisons or specific contrasts
The effect size η² = 0.06 is a population parameter; sample realization may differ

# Load necessary libraries
library(pwr)

# Parameters from the user
eta_squared <- 0.06      # Population eta-squared
k <- 3                   # Number of groups
alpha <- 0.05            # Significance level
target_power <- 0.80     # Target power
balance <- TRUE          # Balanced design

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f effect size
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta^2 / (1 - eta^2))
cohens_f <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

cat("=" %+% strrep("=", 70) %+% "=\n")
cat("ONE-WAY ANOVA SAMPLE SIZE CALCULATION\n")
cat("=" %+% strrep("=", 70) %+% "=\n\n")

cat("INPUT PARAMETERS:\n")
cat("  Number of groups (k):", k, "\n")
cat("  Population eta-squared (η²):", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("  Converted Cohen's f effect size:", sprintf("%.6f", cohens_f), "\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Design: Balanced (equal n per group)\n")
cat("  Test: Omnibus F-test, two-sided upper-tail\n\n")

# Use pwr.anova.test() to find sample size
# The pwr package uses f = Cohen's f
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = cohens_f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

sample_size_exact <- result$n
cat("RESULT FROM pwr.anova.test():\n")
cat("  Exact per-group sample size (n):", sprintf("%.4f", sample_size_exact), "\n\n")

# Round up to the nearest integer for minimum admissible design
n_rounded <- ceiling(sample_size_exact)

cat("MINIMUM INTEGER SAMPLE SIZE:\n")
cat("  Minimum participants per group:", n_rounded, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the selected design
power_at_selected <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = cohens_f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_rounded
)$power

cat("POWER VERIFICATION AT SELECTED DESIGN:\n")
cat("  Achieved power at n =", n_rounded, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_at_selected), "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Meets target?", ifelse(power_at_selected >= target_power, "YES", "NO"), "\n\n")

# Check power at the preceding integer (n_rounded - 1)
if (n_rounded > 1) {
  n_preceding <- n_rounded - 1
  power_at_preceding <- pwr.anova.test(
    k = k,
    f = cohens_f,
    sig.level = alpha,
    n = n_preceding
  )$power
  
  cat("POWER AT PRECEDING ADMISSIBLE DESIGN:\n")
  cat("  Power at n =", n_preceding, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_at_preceding), "\n")
  cat("  Meets target?", ifelse(power_at_preceding >= target_power, "YES", "NO"), "\n\n")
}

# Summary of noncentrality parameter and degrees of freedom
lambda <- n_rounded * k * eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
df1 <- k - 1
df2 <- k * (n_rounded - 1)

cat("TECHNICAL DETAILS FOR SELECTED DESIGN:\n")
cat("  Noncentrality parameter (λ):", sprintf("%.6f", lambda), "\n")
cat("  Numerator degrees of freedom (df1 = k-1):", df1, "\n")
cat("  Denominator degrees of freedom (df2 = k(n-1)):", df2, "\n")
cat("  Total participants:", k * n_rounded, "\n\n")

cat("=" %+% strrep("=", 70) %+% "=\n")

# Return the key result
POWER_AGENT_RESULT_data <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_rounded, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_selected, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "exact_sample_size", value = round(sample_size_exact, 4), unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "cohens_f", value = round(cohens_f, 6), unit = "effect_size"),
    list(metric = "total_participants", value = k * n_rounded, unit = "count")
  )
)

cat("\nFINAL RESULT FOR STRUCTURED REPORTING:\n")
cat("  Primary metric: sample_size\n")
cat("  Value:", n_rounded, "\n")
cat("  Unit: participants_per_group\n")

plan.estimand: Population R-squared in a linear regression model with 3 predictors
plan.hypothesis: H₀: R² = 0 (all regression coefficients equal zero) versus H₁: R² > 0
assumptions: Linear regression model with intercept and exactly 3 predictors
Null hypothesis: R² = 0 (equivalently, all partial regression slopes equal zero)
Test statistic follows noncentral F distribution under the alternative
Normality and homoscedasticity of errors assumed
Fixed predictor values (design matrix is fixed)
One-sided test (testing whether R² > 0)
Population multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, hence population R² = ρ² = 0.09
scientific_notes: Sample size calculation for overall F test of R² in linear regression uses the noncentral F distribution with numerator df = p (number of predictors) and denominator df = N - p - 1
Noncentrality parameter λ relates to R² via: λ = R² × (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
Effect size can be expressed as f² = R² / (1 - R²), where f² ≈ 0.0989 for R² = 0.09
This is a test of whether all predictors collectively explain significant variance, not a test of individual coefficients

answer.summary: For a fixed linear regression model with intercept and 3 predictors testing whether population R-squared differs from zero, with anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30 (hence R² = 0.09), α = 0.05, and target power = 90%, the minimum integer total sample size is 149 participants. This design achieves an actual power of 90.13%. The preceding candidate design (N = 148) yields 89.92% power, confirming that 149 is the smallest admissible size meeting the criterion.
answer.method: Noncentral F test for overall regression. The test statistic under the null hypothesis (R² = 0) follows a central F distribution with df₁ = p = 3 and df₂ = N − p − 1. Under the alternative hypothesis with population R² = 0.09, the test statistic follows a noncentral F distribution with the same degrees of freedom and noncentrality parameter λ = f² × df₂, where f² = R²/(1 − R²) ≈ 0.0989. Power is computed as P(F(df₁, df₂, λ) > F_{crit}(α, df₁, ∞)), where F_{crit} ≈ 2.605 for α = 0.05 and df₁ = 3. A binary search identified the minimum N for which power ≥ 0.90.
assumptions: Fixed linear regression model with intercept and exactly 3 predictors
Null hypothesis: population R² = 0 (all regression slopes equal zero); alternative: R² > 0
Errors are independent and normally distributed with constant variance (homoscedasticity)
Predictor values are fixed (or treated as fixed conditional on their observed values)
Population multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, hence population R² = 0.09
Test is one-sided at α = 0.05 (testing whether any variance is explained)
Inversion uses the noncentral F distribution with no finite-sample correction factors
limitations: No attrition or dropout adjustment; sample size is for enrolled participants with complete data
Calculation assumes the model is correctly specified and that predictors' joint distribution matches the design assumptions
Monte Carlo simulation was not performed; results rely on the noncentral F approximation, which is exact for normal errors under fixed design assumptions
If predictors are random (not fixed), adjustments to the model and power calculation may be needed
The design assumes homogeneity of variance across predictor space; violation of this assumption may reduce actual power

# Parameters
p <- 3                    # number of predictors
rho <- 0.30               # anticipated multiple correlation coefficient
R_squared <- rho^2        # R-squared = 0.09
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
target_power <- 0.90      # desired power
f_squared <- R_squared / (1 - R_squared)  # effect size f²

cat("=== Sample Size Calculation for Linear Regression Overall F Test ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of predictors (p): %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Population multiple correlation (ρ): %.2f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("Population R²: %.4f\n", R_squared))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (f²): %.6f\n", f_squared))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n\n", target_power))

# Critical F value for the numerator df = p at alpha = 0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, p, Inf)
cat(sprintf("Critical F value (df1=%d, df2=Inf): %.6f\n\n", p, f_crit))

# Function to compute power at a given sample size N
compute_power <- function(N, p, f_sq, alpha) {
  df1 <- p
  df2 <- N - p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter: λ = f² × df2
  lambda <- f_sq * df2
  
  # Critical F value
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)
  
  # Power = P(F(df1, df2, λ) > f_crit)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum N that gives power ≥ 0.90
# Start with a reasonable lower bound
N_min <- 5
N_max <- 500
achieved_power <- compute_power(N_max, p, f_squared, alpha)

if (achieved_power < target_power) {
  stop("Sample size of 500 does not achieve target power. Need larger search space.")
}

# Binary search for minimum N
while (N_max - N_min > 1) {
  N_mid <- (N_min + N_max) %/% 2
  power_mid <- compute_power(N_mid, p, f_squared, alpha)
  
  if (power_mid < target_power) {
    N_min <- N_mid
  } else {
    N_max <- N_mid
  }
}

N_opt <- N_max
power_opt <- compute_power(N_opt, p, f_squared, alpha)
N_prev <- N_opt - 1
power_prev <- compute_power(N_prev, p, f_squared, alpha)

cat("=== Results ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum sample size N = %d participants\n", N_opt))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at N = %d: %.6f\n", N_opt, power_opt))
cat(sprintf("Power at preceding design (N = %d): %.6f\n\n", N_prev, power_prev))

# Verify the design
df1 <- p
df2_opt <- N_opt - p - 1
lambda_opt <- f_squared * df2_opt
f_crit_opt <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)

cat("=== Verification ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Numerator df (p): %d\n", df1))
cat(sprintf("Denominator df (N - p - 1): %d\n", df2_opt))
cat(sprintf("Noncentrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", lambda_opt))
cat(sprintf("Critical F value: %.6f\n", f_crit_opt))
cat(sprintf("Test statistic under H₁ ~ F(%d, %d, %.6f)\n", df1, df2_opt, lambda_opt))

# Explicit power computation for final verification
power_explicit <- 1 - pf(f_crit_opt, df1, df2_opt, ncp = lambda_opt)
cat(sprintf("Explicit power calculation: %.6f\n\n", power_explicit))

# Output as JSON for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = N_opt, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = power_opt, unit = "unitless"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = power_prev, unit = "unitless")
  )
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(results, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

assumptions: Linear regression model with intercept and exactly 3 predictors
Null hypothesis: R² = 0 (equivalently, all partial regression slopes equal zero)
Test statistic follows noncentral F distribution under the alternative
Normality and homoscedasticity of errors assumed
Fixed predictor values (design matrix is fixed)
One-sided test (testing whether R² > 0)
Population multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, hence population R² = ρ² = 0.09
scientific_notes: Sample size calculation for overall F test of R² in linear regression uses the noncentral F distribution with numerator df = p (number of predictors) and denominator df = N - p - 1
Noncentrality parameter λ relates to R² via: λ = R² × (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
Effect size can be expressed as f² = R² / (1 - R²), where f² ≈ 0.0989 for R² = 0.09
This is a test of whether all predictors collectively explain significant variance, not a test of individual coefficients

trace.code:
# Parameters
p <- 3                    # number of predictors
rho <- 0.30               # anticipated multiple correlation coefficient
R_squared <- rho^2        # R-squared = 0.09
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
target_power <- 0.90      # desired power
f_squared <- R_squared / (1 - R_squared)  # effect size f²

cat("=== Sample Size Calculation for Linear Regression Overall F Test ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of predictors (p): %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Population multiple correlation (ρ): %.2f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("Population R²: %.4f\n", R_squared))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (f²): %.6f\n", f_squared))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n\n", target_power))

# Critical F value for the numerator df = p at alpha = 0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, p, Inf)
cat(sprintf("Critical F value (df1=%d, df2=Inf): %.6f\n\n", p, f_crit))

# Function to compute power at a given sample size N
compute_power <- function(N, p, f_sq, alpha) {
  df1 <- p
  df2 <- N - p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter: λ = f² × df2
  lambda <- f_sq * df2
  
  # Critical F value
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)
  
  # Power = P(F(df1, df2, λ) > f_crit)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum N that gives power ≥ 0.90
# Start with a reasonable lower bound
N_min <- 5
N_max <- 500
achieved_power <- compute_power(N_max, p, f_squared, alpha)

if (achieved_power < target_power) {
  stop("Sample size of 500 does not achieve target power. Need larger search space.")
}

# Binary search for minimum N
while (N_max - N_min > 1) {
  N_mid <- (N_min + N_max) %/% 2
  power_mid <- compute_power(N_mid, p, f_squared, alpha)
  
  if (power_mid < target_power) {
    N_min <- N_mid
  } else {
    N_max <- N_mid
  }
}

N_opt <- N_max
power_opt <- compute_power(N_opt, p, f_squared, alpha)
N_prev <- N_opt - 1
power_prev <- compute_power(N_prev, p, f_squared, alpha)

cat("=== Results ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum sample size N = %d participants\n", N_opt))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at N = %d: %.6f\n", N_opt, power_opt))
cat(sprintf("Power at preceding design (N = %d): %.6f\n\n", N_prev, power_prev))

# Verify the design
df1 <- p
df2_opt <- N_opt - p - 1
lambda_opt <- f_squared * df2_opt
f_crit_opt <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)

cat("=== Verification ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Numerator df (p): %d\n", df1))
cat(sprintf("Denominator df (N - p - 1): %d\n", df2_opt))
cat(sprintf("Noncentrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", lambda_opt))
cat(sprintf("Critical F value: %.6f\n", f_crit_opt))
cat(sprintf("Test statistic under H₁ ~ F(%d, %d, %.6f)\n", df1, df2_opt, lambda_opt))

# Explicit power computation for final verification
power_explicit <- 1 - pf(f_crit_opt, df1, df2_opt, ncp = lambda_opt)
cat(sprintf("Explicit power calculation: %.6f\n\n", power_explicit))

# Output as JSON for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = N_opt, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = power_opt, unit = "unitless"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = power_prev, unit = "unitless")
  )
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(results, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

plan.hypothesis: Under expected shrinkage (0.95) with 10 candidate predictors and anticipated Cox-Snell R-squared 0.12 at prevalence 0.20, the sample size will be sufficient such that the absolute difference between apparent and adjusted Nagelkerke R-squared remains ≤0.05 and the average outcome-risk margin of error ≤0.05

parameters.name: Target average outcome-risk margin of error

assumptions: Prediction model is binary logistic regression with intercept only modification
Cox-Snell R-squared 0.12 reflects true model performance before shrinkage
Shrinkage factor 0.95 applied uniformly to apparent model performance
Nagelkerke R-squared scale used for absolute precision criterion (standard for binary models)
95% confidence level governs precision margin calculation
Default pmsampsize absolute precision criteria applied (max R-squared apparent-vs-adjusted difference)

For verification at the returned sample size, is a closed-form analytical calculation acceptable, or is simulation-based validation preferred?

Average outcome-risk margin of error references predictive accuracy on probability scale; sensitivity analysis recommended if model is deployed in populations with substantially different outcome prevalence

answer.summary: For a one-sample t-test with n=25 participants, testing H₀: μ = 0 versus H₁: μ = 0.2 (one-sided, directional) at α = 0.05 with σ = 0.5 units, the statistical power is 0.617258997440687 (probability). This represents the probability of detecting a 0.2-unit increase from the null mean when the true effect exists, corresponding to Cohen's d = 0.4. The result was computed analytically using the non-central t distribution and verified via simulation (100,000 replications).
answer.method: One-sample t-test power via non-central t distribution. Under the alternative hypothesis H₁: μ = 0.2 with σ = 0.5, the test statistic follows a non-central t distribution with df = 24 and non-centrality parameter λ = √n × d = √25 × 0.4 = 2.0. The one-sided critical value is t₀.₀₅,₂₄ = 1.7109. Power = P(T₂₄ > 1.7109 | λ = 2.0) = 0.617258997440687. The analytic solution was independently verified through simulation under the same data-generating model (normal outcomes with mean 0.2 and SD 0.5).

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# Parameters
n <- 25                    # sample size (participants)
alpha <- 0.05              # significance level
effect_size <- 0.2         # mean difference to detect
sd <- 0.5                  # standard deviation
null_mean <- 0             # null hypothesis mean

# Calculate non-centrality parameter
# ncp = sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)
ncp <- sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)

# For a one-sided test, we compute:
# Power = P(t_{n-1} > t_{critical} | ncp)
# where t_critical is the critical value at alpha level with df = n-1

df <- n - 1                # degrees of freedom

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of exceeding the critical value under the alternative
power <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp)

# Display results
cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n):           %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Null hypothesis:           μ = %.1f\n", null_mean))
cat(sprintf("Alternative hypothesis:   μ = %.1f (one-sided, directional)\n", effect_size))
cat(sprintf("Standard deviation (σ):    %.1f units\n", sd))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α):    %.2f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom:        %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter:  %.4f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value:          %.4f\n", t_critical))
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d:                 %.2f\n", effect_size / sd))
cat(sprintf("\nPower (probability):       %.6f\n", power))

# Independent verification of one-sample t-test power
# Using a fresh calculation without relying on candidate's code

# Study parameters (from original request)
n <- 25
alpha <- 0.05
effect_size_mean <- 0.2  # mean under H1
sd_pop <- 0.5
null_mean <- 0
sidedness <- "one-sided"  # directional test, H1: μ > 0

# Step 1: Compute Cohen's d
cohens_d <- (effect_size_mean - null_mean) / sd_pop
cat("Step 1: Effect Size\n")
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d = (%.1f - %.1f) / %.1f = %.4f\n", effect_size_mean, null_mean, sd_pop, cohens_d))

# Step 2: Compute non-centrality parameter (ncp)
# Under H1, the t-statistic is distributed as t(df, ncp) where ncp = sqrt(n) * d
df <- n - 1
ncp <- sqrt(n) * cohens_d
cat("\nStep 2: Non-centrality Parameter\n")
cat(sprintf("df = n - 1 = %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("ncp = sqrt(n) × Cohen's d = sqrt(%d) × %.4f = %.4f\n", n, cohens_d, ncp))

# Step 3: Find critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For one-sided test with H1: μ > 0, we use the right tail
# t_crit = t_{1-α, df} = t_{0.95, 24}
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
cat("\nStep 3: Critical Value (One-Sided)\n")
cat(sprintf("For α = %.2f (one-sided), critical t = t_{%.2f, %d} = %.6f\n", 
            alpha, 1-alpha, df, t_crit))

# Step 4: Power calculation
# Power = P(T > t_crit | T ~ t(df, ncp))
# This is evaluated using the non-central t CDF
power_from_nct <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
cat("\nStep 4: Power Calculation\n")
cat(sprintf("Power = P(T > %.6f | T ~ t(%d, ncp=%.4f))\n", t_crit, df, ncp))
cat(sprintf("Power = 1 - P(T ≤ %.6f | T ~ t(%d, ncp=%.4f))\n", t_crit, df, ncp))
cat(sprintf("Power = 1 - Φ_{nct}(%.6f; df=%d, ncp=%.4f)\n", t_crit, df, ncp))
cat(sprintf("Power = %.15f\n", power_from_nct))

# Step 5: Verify using simulation with different random seed
set.seed(9999)  # Different seed from candidate
n_sim <- 150000
test_results <- numeric(n_sim)

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # Generate sample under H1
  y <- rnorm(n, mean = effect_size_mean, sd = sd_pop)
  
  # Compute t-statistic (note: we don't know population SD, so use sample SD)
  sample_mean <- mean(y)
  sample_se <- sd(y) / sqrt(n)
  t_stat <- (sample_mean - null_mean) / sample_se
  
  test_results[i] <- t_stat
}

# Count how many exceed critical value
power_sim <- mean(test_results > t_crit)
sim_se <- sqrt(power_sim * (1 - power_sim) / n_sim)
sim_ci_lower <- power_sim - 1.96 * sim_se
sim_ci_upper <- power_sim + 1.96 * sim_se

cat("\nStep 5: Simulation Verification (Independent Seed)\n")

cat(sprintf("Replications: %d\n", n_sim))
cat(sprintf("Simulated Power: %.10f\n", power_sim))
cat(sprintf("Simulation SE: %.10f\n", sim_se))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.10f, %.10f]\n", sim_ci_lower, sim_ci_upper))

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# Parameters
n <- 25                    # sample size (participants)
alpha <- 0.05              # significance level
effect_size <- 0.2         # mean difference to detect
sd <- 0.5                  # standard deviation
null_mean <- 0             # null hypothesis mean

# Calculate non-centrality parameter
# ncp = sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)
ncp <- sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)

# For a one-sided test, we compute:
# Power = P(t_{n-1} > t_{critical} | ncp)
# where t_critical is the critical value at alpha level with df = n-1

df <- n - 1                # degrees of freedom

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of exceeding the critical value under the alternative
power <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp)

# Display results
cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n):           %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Null hypothesis:           μ = %.1f\n", null_mean))
cat(sprintf("Alternative hypothesis:   μ = %.1f (one-sided, directional)\n", effect_size))
cat(sprintf("Standard deviation (σ):    %.1f units\n", sd))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α):    %.2f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom:        %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter:  %.4f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value:          %.4f\n", t_critical))
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d:                 %.2f\n", effect_size / sd))
cat(sprintf("\nPower (probability):       %.6f\n", power))

# Round to reasonable precision for reporting
power_rounded <- round(power, 4)
cat(sprintf("Power (rounded to 4 dp):   %.4f\n", power_rounded))

# Output for structured result
library(jsonlite)
result <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )
)

# Independent verification of one-sample t-test power
# Using a fresh calculation without relying on candidate's code

# Study parameters (from original request)
n <- 25
alpha <- 0.05
effect_size_mean <- 0.2  # mean under H1
sd_pop <- 0.5
null_mean <- 0
sidedness <- "one-sided"  # directional test, H1: μ > 0

# Step 1: Compute Cohen's d
cohens_d <- (effect_size_mean - null_mean) / sd_pop
cat("Step 1: Effect Size\n")
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d = (%.1f - %.1f) / %.1f = %.4f\n", effect_size_mean, null_mean, sd_pop, cohens_d))

# Step 2: Compute non-centrality parameter (ncp)
# Under H1, the t-statistic is distributed as t(df, ncp) where ncp = sqrt(n) * d
df <- n - 1
ncp <- sqrt(n) * cohens_d
cat("\nStep 2: Non-centrality Parameter\n")
cat(sprintf("df = n - 1 = %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("ncp = sqrt(n) × Cohen's d = sqrt(%d) × %.4f = %.4f\n", n, cohens_d, ncp))

# Step 3: Find critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For one-sided test with H1: μ > 0, we use the right tail
# t_crit = t_{1-α, df} = t_{0.95, 24}
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
cat("\nStep 3: Critical Value (One-Sided)\n")
cat(sprintf("For α = %.2f (one-sided), critical t = t_{%.2f, %d} = %.6f\n", 
            alpha, 1-alpha, df, t_crit))

# Step 4: Power calculation
# Power = P(T > t_crit | T ~ t(df, ncp))
# This is evaluated using the non-central t CDF
power_from_nct <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
cat("\nStep 4: Power Calculation\n")
cat(sprintf("Power = P(T > %.6f | T ~ t(%d, ncp=%.4f))\n", t_crit, df, ncp))
cat(sprintf("Power = 1 - P(T ≤ %.6f | T ~ t(%d, ncp=%.4f))\n", t_crit, df, ncp))
cat(sprintf("Power = 1 - Φ_{nct}(%.6f; df=%d, ncp=%.4f)\n", t_crit, df, ncp))
cat(sprintf("Power = %.15f\n", power_from_nct))

# Step 5: Verify using simulation with different random seed
set.seed(9999)  # Different seed from candidate
n_sim <- 150000
test_results <- numeric(n_sim)

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # Generate sample under H1
  y <- rnorm(n, mean = effect_size_mean, sd = sd_pop)
  
  # Compute t-statistic (note: we don't know population SD, so use sample SD)
  sample_mean <- mean(y)
  sample_se <- sd(y) / sqrt(n)
  t_stat <- (sample_mean - null_mean) / sample_se
  
  test_results[i] <- t_stat
}

# Count how many exceed critical value
power_sim <- mean(test_results > t_crit)
sim_se <- sqrt(power_sim * (1 - power_sim) / n_sim)
sim_ci_lower <- power_sim - 1.96 * sim_se
sim_ci_upper <- power_sim + 1.96 * sim_se

cat("\nStep 5: Simulation Verification (Independent Seed)\n")
cat(sprintf("Seed: 9999\n"))
cat(sprintf("Replications: %d\n", n_sim))
cat(sprintf("Simulated Power: %.10f\n", power_sim))
cat(sprintf("Simulation SE: %.10f\n", sim_se))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.10f, %.10f]\n", sim_ci_lower, sim_ci_upper))

# Check if analytic result falls within simulation CI
within_ci <- (power_from_nct >= sim_ci_lower) && (power_from_nct <= sim_ci_upper)
cat(sprintf("\nAnalytic power (%.15f) within sim CI? %s\n", power_from_nct, 
            ifelse(within_ci, "YES", "NO")))

# Difference between methods
diff <- abs(power_from_nct - power_sim)
cat(sprintf("Absolute difference: %.10f\n", diff))
cat(sprintf("Relative difference: %.4f%%\n", 100 * diff / power_from_nct))

# Final verification: Check using pwr package as third method
library(pwr)
pwr_result <- pwr.t.test(n = n, d = cohens_d, sig.level = alpha, 
                         type = "one.sample", alternative = "greater")

cat("\nStep 6: Cross-check with pwr package\n")
cat(sprintf("pwr.t.test result: power = %.15f\n", pwr_result$power))
cat(sprintf("Match with analytic (pt)? %s\n", 
            ifelse(abs(pwr_result$power - power_from_nct) < 1e-10, "YES", "NO")))

# Summary
cat("\n" %+% "="*60 %+% "\n")
cat("INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION SUMMARY\n")
cat("="*60 %+% "\n")
cat(sprintf("Analytic (non-central t):  %.15f\n", power_from_nct))
cat(sprintf("Simulation (seed=9999):    %.15f\n", power_sim))
cat(sprintf("pwr package:               %.15f\n", pwr_result$power))
cat(sprintf("\nAll three methods agree? %s\n", 
            ifelse(max(abs(power_from_nct - power_sim), 
                       abs(power_from_nct - pwr_result$power)) < 0.002, 
                   "YES", "NO")))
cat(sprintf("Candidate answer value:    %.15f\n", 0.617258997440687))
cat(sprintf("Match with our analytic?   %s\n", 
            ifelse(abs(0.617258997440687 - power_from_nct) < 1e-14, "YES", "NO")))

# Output JSON for system
library(jsonlite)
check_result <- list(
  analytic_power = power_from_nct,
  simulation_power = power_sim,
  pwr_package_power = pwr_result$power,
  candidate_answer = 0.617258997440687,
  analytic_matches_candidate = abs(0.617258997440687 - power_from_nct) < 1e-14,
  simulation_ci = c(sim_ci_lower, sim_ci_upper),
  analytic_in_sim_ci = within_ci,

cat(sprintf("\nAnalytic power (%.15f) within sim CI? %s\n", power_from_nct, 
            ifelse(within_ci, "YES", "NO")))

            ifelse(abs(0.617258997440687 - power_from_nct) < 1e-14, "YES", "NO")))

# Evidence e1; success=true

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# Parameters
n <- 25                    # sample size (participants)
alpha <- 0.05              # significance level
effect_size <- 0.2         # mean difference to detect
sd <- 0.5                  # standard deviation
null_mean <- 0             # null hypothesis mean

# Calculate non-centrality parameter
# ncp = sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)
ncp <- sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)

# For a one-sided test, we compute:
# Power = P(t_{n-1} > t_{critical} | ncp)
# where t_critical is the critical value at alpha level with df = n-1

df <- n - 1                # degrees of freedom

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of exceeding the critical value under the alternative
power <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp)

# Display results
cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n):           %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Null hypothesis:           μ = %.1f\n", null_mean))
cat(sprintf("Alternative hypothesis:   μ = %.1f (one-sided, directional)\n", effect_size))
cat(sprintf("Standard deviation (σ):    %.1f units\n", sd))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α):    %.2f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom:        %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter:  %.4f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value:          %.4f\n", t_critical))
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d:                 %.2f\n", effect_size / sd))
cat(sprintf("\nPower (probability):       %.6f\n", power))

# Round to reasonable precision for reporting
power_rounded <- round(power, 4)
cat(sprintf("Power (rounded to 4 dp):   %.4f\n", power_rounded))

# Output for structured result
library(jsonlite)
result <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

library(pwr)

# Method 1: Using pwr package
# For one-sample t-test, effect size is Cohen's d
n <- 25
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05

# Cohen's d
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

# pwr.t.test for one-sample t-test
# Note: alternative="greater" for one-sided test with H1: μ > 0
power_pwr <- pwr.t.test(n = n, d = cohens_d, sig.level = alpha, 
                         type = "one.sample", alternative = "greater")

cat("Method 1: pwr package\n")
cat("=====================\n")
print(power_pwr)
cat("\n")

# Method 2: Direct calculation using t distribution
# Power = P(T > t_critical | ncp = sqrt(n) * d)
df <- n - 1
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
ncp <- sqrt(n) * cohens_d
power_direct <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("Method 2: Direct non-central t distribution\n")
cat("============================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d:                 %.4f\n", cohens_d))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter:  %.4f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value (df=%d):   %.4f\n", df, t_critical))
cat(sprintf("Power:                     %.10f\n", power_direct))
cat("\n")

# Method 3: Confirmation via simulation
set.seed(20250127)
nsim <- 100000
n <- 25
mean_null <- 0
mean_alt <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05

# Generate data under H1 and test

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  y <- rnorm(n, mean = mean_alt, sd = sd)
  t_stats[i] <- (mean(y) - mean_null) / (sd(y) / sqrt(n))
}

# Critical value
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = n - 1)

# Proportion of tests exceeding critical value

cat(sprintf("Direct calculation:        %.10f\n", power_direct))
cat(sprintf("Simulation:                %.10f\n", power_sim))
cat(sprintf("\nRounded to 4 decimal places: %.4f\n", round(power_direct, 4)))

  )
)

answer.method: Noncentral F-test for omnibus linear regression. The noncentrality parameter λ = (n × R²) / (1 − R²) where R² = ρ² = 0.09. The test statistic follows F(df₁ = 3, df₂ = 76) under H₀ and F(df₁ = 3, df₂ = 76, λ = 7.912) under H₁. Power is calculated as P(F > F_crit | H₁), where F_crit is the critical value from the central F distribution at α = 0.05.

limitations: Power estimate assumes perfect specification of the effect size; power is sensitive to misspecification of ρ

# Power calculation for omnibus F-test in linear regression
# H0: R^2 = 0 vs H1: R^2 ≠ 0
# 
# Parameters:
n <- 80               # sample size (participants)
rho <- 0.30           # anticipated multiple correlation coefficient
k <- 3                # number of predictors (excluding intercept)
alpha <- 0.05         # significance level (two-tailed)

# Derived quantities:
R2 <- rho^2           # R-squared (effect size)
df_num <- k           # numerator df (number of predictors)
df_den <- n - k - 1   # denominator df (n - p - 1 where p = number of predictors)

# Noncentrality parameter for F distribution
# λ = (n * R²) / (1 - R²)
lambda <- (n * R2) / (1 - R2)

# Critical F-value from central F distribution at alpha = 0.05 (two-tailed)
F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df_num, df2 = df_den, ncp = 0)

# Power = P(F > F_crit | H1 true) using noncentral F distribution
# This is the probability of rejecting H0 when the true R = 0.30
power <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df_num, df2 = df_den, ncp = lambda)

# Summary output
cat("================== Linear Regression Power Calculation ==================\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H0: R² = 0 vs H1: R² ≠ 0 (omnibus F-test)\n")
cat("Method: Noncentral F-test\n\n")
cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Sample size (n):                 %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("  Number of predictors (k):       %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  Intercept:                       1 (included in model)\n"))
cat("  Total model parameters:          ", k + 1, "(intercept + 3 predictors)\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Effect Size & Test Specification:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ):  %.4f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("  R-squared (effect size):                %.4f\n", R2))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α):                 %.4f (two-tailed)\n", alpha))
cat("\n")
cat("Degrees of Freedom:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Numerator df:                    %d\n", df_num))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df:                  %d\n", df_den))
cat("\n")
cat("Statistical Test:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Noncentrality parameter (λ):    %.6f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("  Critical F-value (F_crit):      %.6f\n", F_crit))
cat("\n")
cat("POWER RESULTS:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Power (1 - β):                   %.6f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  Power (%% probability):          %.2f%%\n", power * 100))
cat("==========================================================================\n")

# Return structured result
result <- list(
  power = power,
  power_pct = power * 100,
  n = n,
  rho = rho,
  R2 = R2,
  k = k,
  df_num = df_num,
  df_den = df_den,
  lambda = lambda,
  F_crit = F_crit,
  alpha = alpha
)

# Emit result in required format
library(jsonlite)
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
cat("\n")

# Install and load pwr package for power analysis
if (!requireNamespace("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr")
}
library(pwr)

# Define parameters
effect_size <- 0.2 / 0.5  # Cohen's d = mean_difference / SD
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
alternative <- "greater"  # one-sided test

# Use pwr.t.test for one-sample t-test
# Type "one.sample" requires effect size as Cohen's d
result <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,  # Solve for n
  d = effect_size,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = alternative
)

# Extract the sample size (continuous solution)
continuous_n <- result$n
print(paste("Continuous sample size:", continuous_n))

# Round up to next integer (smallest integer achieving target power)
min_n_integer <- ceiling(continuous_n)
print(paste("Minimum integer sample size:", min_n_integer))

# Verify achieved power at this integer sample size
verification <- pwr.t.test(
  n = min_n_integer,
  d = effect_size,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = alternative
)
achieved_power <- verification$power
print(paste("Achieved power at n =", min_n_integer, ":", round(achieved_power, 6)))

# Also check power at n-1 to confirm this is the minimum
if (min_n_integer > 1) {
  previous <- pwr.t.test(
    n = min_n_integer - 1,
    d = effect_size,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "one.sample",
    alternative = alternative
  )
  power_previous <- previous$power
  print(paste("Power at n =", min_n_integer - 1, ":", round(power_previous, 6)))
}

# Output results in required format
results_df <- data.frame(
  metric = c("sample_size", "achieved_power", "effect_size_cohens_d", "alpha", "target_power"),
  value = c(min_n_integer, achieved_power, effect_size, alpha, target_power),
  unit = c("participants_total", "probability", "unitless", "probability", "probability")
)

print("\nSummary:")
print(results_df)

# Emit result in required format
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = results_df),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
))

# H0: mu_treatment = mu_control vs. H1: mu_treatment > mu_control

sided <- "one.sided"        # direction: one-sided test

# Use stats::power.t.test for two-sample t-test with equal variances

  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",

      unit = "probability"

# H0: mu_treatment = mu_control vs. H1: mu_treatment > mu_control
# Two independent normal groups with equal variances

alpha <- 0.05               # significance level
sided <- "one.sided"        # direction: one-sided test

# Use stats::power.t.test for two-sample t-test with equal variances
# effect = delta / sigma (Cohen's d)

  n = n_per_group,
  delta = expected_difference,
  sd = common_sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = sided
)

# Extract power
power <- power_result$power

# Calculate degrees of freedom for reference

cat("Derived Quantities:\n")

cat(sprintf("  Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))

expected_difference <- 4.3  # dBA
common_sd <- 7.8            # dBA
n_per_group <- 32           # participants per group
alpha <- 0.05               # significance level
total_n <- 2 * n_per_group

# Compute power using power.t.test
power_result <- power.t.test(
  n = n_per_group,
  delta = expected_difference,
  sd = common_sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

# Extract the power value
power_value <- power_result$power

df <- total_n - 2
lambda <- expected_difference / (common_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group))
t_crit <- qt(p = 1 - alpha, df = df)
power_verify <- 1 - pt(q = t_crit, df = df, ncp = lambda)

# Standardized effect size (Cohen's d)

# Create structured result

      metric = "power",

      unit = "probability"

expected_difference <- 4.3  # dBA

n_per_group <- 32           # participants
alpha <- 0.05               # significance level

# Non-centrality parameter (λ)
# For two-sample t-test: λ = δ / (σ√(2/n)) where δ is expected difference
lambda <- expected_difference / (common_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group))

# Degrees of freedom
df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2

# Critical value for one-sided test at α = 0.05
# For one-sided test (right-tailed): t_crit = t_{α,df}

# Power is P(t > t_crit | H1 true) = P(t_nc(λ, df) > t_crit)
# where t_nc is non-central t distribution
power_nc <- 1 - pt(q = t_crit, df = df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)

cat("=====================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter (λ): %.4f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Critical value (t_{1-α,df}): %.4f\n", t_crit))
cat(sprintf("Power (1 - P(t ≤ t_crit | λ)): %.6f\n", power_nc))
cat("=====================================================\n")

cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality result: %.6f\n", power_nc))

answer.method: Fixed-effects F-test for main effect in factorial ANOVA with noncentrality parameter derived from partial eta-squared. Power was computed as P(F > F_critical) for F ~ F(2, df_error, λ). Integer search identified the smallest n giving power ≥ 0.80.
